claims.title: The megaliths of Bouar are raised
claims.summary: Farmers near Bouar in the west erected multi-ton standing stones (tazunu), among the most important prehistoric monuments in Central Africa and evidence of organised Neolithic communities.

sources.label: History of the Central African Republic

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-3500bce-the-megaliths-of-bouar-are-raised, claim TL:CAF:event:3500bce:the-megaliths-of-bouar-are-raised, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ironworking and migration
claims.summary: Ubangian, Central Sudanic and Bantu-speaking peoples settled the watershed and ironworking spread, laying down the ethnic patchwork of Gbaya, Banda, Zande, Nzakara and others.

sources.label: History of the Central African Republic

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1000bce-ironworking-and-migration, claim TL:CAF:event:1000bce:ironworking-and-migration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zande and Bandia kingdoms expand
claims.summary: Under the Avongara nobility the Zande spread across the south-east, while the Bandia clan founded Ubangi River states including the Nzakara kingdom and the sultanate of Bangassou.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1700-zande-and-bandia-kingdoms-expand, claim TL:CAF:event:1700:zande-and-bandia-kingdoms-expand, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dar al-Kuti founded under Wadai
claims.summary: The sultanate of Dar al-Kuti was established as a tributary of Dar Runga and ultimately of Wadai, becoming a staging ground for slave raids into the Banda and Nzakara lands to the south.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1830-dar-al-kuti-founded-under-wadai, claim TL:CAF:event:1830:dar-al-kuti-founded-under-wadai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Al-Zubayr installs al-Sanusi at Dar al-Kuti
claims.summary: The Sudanese warlord Rabih az-Zubayr (al-Zubayr) deposed Kobur and installed Muhammad al-Sanusi, who from his base at Ndélé intensified the razzias that depopulated much of the Ubangi region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1890-al-zubayr-installs-al-sanusi-at-dar-al-kuti, claim TL:CAF:event:1890:al-zubayr-installs-al-sanusi-at-dar-al-kuti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France founds Bangui
claims.summary: French forces established a post at Bangui on the Ubangi River, the base from which they extended control over the territory that became the colony of Ubangi-Shari.

sources.label: History of the Central African Republic

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1889-france-founds-bangui, claim TL:CAF:event:1889:france-founds-bangui, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Concessionary companies take over
claims.summary: France leased huge tracts of Ubangi-Shari to private companies such as the Company of the Upper Ubangi Sultanates, whose militias exacted rubber and ivory through brutal forced labour.

sources.label: Company of the Upper Ubangi Sultanates
The Economic History of the Central African Republic

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1899-concessionary-companies-take-over, claim TL:CAF:event:1899:concessionary-companies-take-over, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of al-Sanusi of Dar al-Kuti
claims.summary: French forces killed Muhammad al-Sanusi at Ndélé, ending the slave-raiding sultanate of Dar al-Kuti; his successor's resistance was suppressed by 1912.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1911-death-of-al-sanusi-of-dar-al-kuti, claim TL:CAF:event:1911:death-of-al-sanusi-of-dar-al-kuti, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kongo-Wara rebellion
claims.summary: The Gbaya prophet Karinou led a mass revolt against forced labour and railway recruitment; the French killed him in December 1928 and crushed the uprising by 1931, with thousands dead.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1928-kongo-wara-rebellion, claim TL:CAF:event:1928:kongo-wara-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Boganda founds MESAN
claims.summary: Barthélemy Boganda, the territory's first deputy to the French National Assembly, founded the Movement for the Social Evolution of Black Africa, the engine of Central African nationalism.

sources.label: Movement for the Social Evolution of Black Africa (MESAN)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1949-boganda-founds-mesan, claim TL:CAF:event:1949:boganda-founds-mesan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Boganda
claims.summary: Boganda, who had proclaimed the autonomous republic in December 1958 and championed a 'United States of Latin Africa', died in a plane crash months before independence; David Dacko succeeded him.

sources.label: Remembering the national hero of the Central African Republic who died in a plane crash before independence

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1959-death-of-boganda, claim TL:CAF:event:1959:death-of-boganda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence from France
claims.summary: The Central African Republic became fully independent, with David Dacko as its first president and Bangui as its capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-from-france, claim TL:CAF:event:1960:independence-from-france, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ubangi-Shari joins French Equatorial Africa
claims.summary: The dependency France set up in 1894 is folded into the federation governed from Brazzaville, a structure that lasted until independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1910-ubangi-shari-joins-french-equatorial-africa, claim TL:CAF:event:1910:ubangi-shari-joins-french-equatorial-africa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: An assembly, and a seat in Paris
claims.summary: The territory gains its own assembly and representation in the French parliament; Barthélemy Boganda becomes the first Central African elected to it.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1946-an-assembly-and-a-seat-in-paris, claim TL:CAF:event:1946:an-assembly-and-a-seat-in-paris, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Self-government under Boganda
claims.summary: Ubangi-Shari achieves self-government within French Equatorial Africa with Boganda as prime minister, months before his death in an air crash.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1958-self-government-under-boganda, claim TL:CAF:event:1958:self-government-under-boganda, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bokassa seizes power
claims.summary: Army commander Jean-Bédel Bokassa overthrew President David Dacko in the Saint-Sylvestre coup, beginning more than a decade of personal rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1966-bokassa-seizes-power, claim TL:CAF:event:1966:bokassa-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coronation of Emperor Bokassa I
claims.summary: Having declared the Central African Empire in 1976, Bokassa crowned himself emperor in a lavish ceremony costing about US$20 million while the country remained among the world's poorest.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1977-coronation-of-emperor-bokassa-i, claim TL:CAF:event:1977:coronation-of-emperor-bokassa-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Killing of schoolchildren
claims.summary: Protests against compulsory school uniforms ended in the massacre of scores of detained children and students in Bangui, an atrocity widely linked to Bokassa that hastened the end of his rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1979-killing-of-schoolchildren, claim TL:CAF:event:1979:killing-of-schoolchildren, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France overthrows Bokassa
claims.summary: A French military operation (Barracuda) deposed Bokassa and restored David Dacko; Bokassa fled into exile and was later tried and convicted.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1979-france-overthrows-bokassa, claim TL:CAF:event:1979:france-overthrows-bokassa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bozizé seizes power
claims.summary: After coups by André Kolingba (1981) and an elected interlude under Ange-Félix Patassé, army chief François Bozizé overthrew Patassé, continuing the cycle of armed takeovers.

sources.label: History of the Central African Republic

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-2003-bozize-seizes-power, claim TL:CAF:event:2003:bozize-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Patassé ends twelve years of military rule
claims.summary: Ange-Félix Patassé wins the presidency in elections that close the era opened by Bokassa and continued by his successors.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-1993-patasse-ends-twelve-years-of-military-rule, claim TL:CAF:event:1993:patasse-ends-twelve-years-of-military-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Séléka captures Bangui
claims.summary: The Séléka rebel coalition seized the capital and ousted President Bozizé; its leader Michel Djotodia declared himself president, the country's first Muslim head of state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-2013-seleka-captures-bangui, claim TL:CAF:event:2013:seleka-captures-bangui, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sectarian civil war erupts
claims.summary: Reprisals between Séléka and the anti-balaka militias spiralled into sectarian massacres; attacks in Bangui in early December 2013 killed more than a thousand civilians.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-2013-sectarian-civil-war-erupts, claim TL:CAF:event:2013:sectarian-civil-war-erupts, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN establishes MINUSCA
claims.summary: After French and African Union deployments, the UN Security Council authorised the MINUSCA peacekeeping mission in April 2014; it assumed responsibility in September, alongside interim president Catherine Samba-Panza.

sources.label: MINUSCA — United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-2014-un-establishes-minusca, claim TL:CAF:event:2014:un-establishes-minusca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Khartoum peace agreement
claims.summary: President Touadéra's government and fourteen armed groups signed a peace accord in Khartoum, but implementation was partial and fighting soon resumed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-2019-khartoum-peace-agreement, claim TL:CAF:event:2019:khartoum-peace-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: CPC offensive and Wagner
claims.summary: A rebel coalition (the CPC) attacked around the December 2020 elections; the government, increasingly backed by Russian Wagner Group mercenaries deployed from 2018, pushed it back with MINUSCA's help.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Central African Republic: From the megaliths of Bouar to a fragile peace at the heart of Africa", terralore.co/country/CAF/chronicle#ev-2020-cpc-offensive-and-wagner, claim TL:CAF:event:2020:cpc-offensive-and-wagner, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
